citations.title: Facility licensure
citations.requirement: APD licenses group home facilities (4-15 residents) and foster care facilities (3 or fewer). The statute requires Level 2 screening of the applicant, managers, supervisors and direct service staff (subsec. (5)). It requires proof of financial ability (subsec. (6)) and a comprehensive emergency management plan (subsec. (8)). It requires an annual sworn statement of costs for APD-funded clients (subsec. (10)). APD cannot fund an unlicensed facility.

citations.title: License Application and Renewal Procedures (amended 3-26-26)
citations.requirement: Each home has its own license (subsec. (8)). The application is complete only with all documents, screenings and a satisfactory inspection. Deficiencies must be corrected before the license issues. Renewals are due at least 45 days before expiration (subsec. (4)); late or incomplete renewals are treated as initial applications. Give APD 30 days' written notice before closing a home (subsec. (13)).

citations.title: Length of Licenses
citations.requirement: Residential facility licenses are issued for one year.

citations.title: Agency Monitoring and Oversight
citations.requirement: APD monitors licensed homes at least monthly, including one weekend visit a year (subsec. (4)). It may request proof of ability to operate 60 days without state payment (subsec. (5)). It reviews the home on site within 30 days after the first admission (subsec. (8)).

citations.title: Licensed Residential Facility Capacity
citations.requirement: APD sets licensed capacity and resident characteristics. Capacity changes must be requested 30 days ahead with a passed fire inspection and zoning compliance (subsec. (1)(d)). Census changes must be reported in writing (subsec. (2)). Serve only residents whose characteristics match the license (subsec. (3)).

citations.title: General Residential Facility Standards
citations.requirement: Physical plant standards: no mobile homes; maximum 2 residents per bedroom for homes first licensed on or after 7/1/2014; bedroom space of at least 80 sq ft (single) or 60 sq ft per person (shared); one toilet, sink and tub/shower per 3 residents; 35 sq ft of living/dining space per household member; hot water at or below 120°F; smoke and CO detectors; restricted access to water hazards; secured hazardous chemicals; meal provisions; an office area with secure records storage.

citations.title: Group Home Facility Standards
citations.requirement: The facility operator needs 90 college credits in a related field, or a high school diploma plus 3 years of disability experience. The operator must be on site or on call at all times, with a designated backup (subsecs. (2)-(3)). The home needs a designated office area (subsec. (4)).

citations.title: Staffing Requirements for Residential Facilities (amended 3-26-26)
citations.requirement: The licensee must employ adequate staff for the number and characteristics of residents, even above the minimum (subsec. (1)). DSP qualifications are in subsec. (2): age 18+; ch. 435 / s. 393.0655 screening; high school diploma or equivalent; 1 year of experience or 30 semester hours / 45 quarter hours / 720 classroom hours of related training. Subsec. (2)(f)-(h) sets the supervised 90-day alternative, written notice to the Regional Office within 5 days of hire, and a performance evaluation within 120 days. Subsec. (3) sets required skills. Subsec. (4) covers fitness for duty, driver standards (no qualifying violation in 3 years, annual driving-history update) and the annual FDLE sexual offender/predator database check within one mile. Subsec. (5) covers investigations. Subsec. (6) covers personnel records, job descriptions, weekly schedules posted one week ahead and actual schedules kept 6 months; copies go to APD within 3 calendar days. Subsec. (7) sets training: Direct Care Core Competencies and classroom CPR/first aid within 90 days, Zero Tolerance before services with refresher every 3 years, HIV/AIDS within 90 days, behavior-plan training by a certified behavior analyst, and Ch. 65G-8 compliance. Training records are kept 3 years.

citations.title: Resident Care and Supervision Standards (amended 3-26-26)
citations.requirement: Subsec. (1) covers care standards, the Bill of Rights, written house rules and follow-up of medical appointments. Subsec. (2) requires community activity opportunities. Subsec. (3) covers admission/termination criteria, notice to APD before accepting each new resident and a census change report within 5 calendar days. It also covers transfer approval and the property inventory. Subsec. (4) covers resident funds. Subsec. (5) covers resident records: contents, updated within 30 days of new information, retained 6 years, copies to APD within 2 calendar days. Subsec. (6) requires at least one staff present at all times residents are in the facility, with limited exceptions by Regional Office-approved plan. Subsec. (7) covers video monitoring. Subsec. (8) covers behavioral interventions. Subsec. (9) covers the sexual activity policy and Safety Plan safeguards. Subsec. (10) covers solicitation. Subsec. (11) covers first aid. Subsec. (12) covers medication. Subsec. (13) covers specialized equipment. Subsec. (14) covers transportation. Subsec. (15) covers staff communication.

citations.title: Fire and Emergency Procedures (amended 3-26-26)
citations.requirement: Subsec. (1) requires emergency numbers at every phone extension. Subsec. (2) requires an annual fire inspection under ch. 69A-38 and an approved inspection before initial licensure or renewal. Subsec. (3) requires monthly fire drills, with records kept 1 year and no drills between midnight and 5:00 a.m. Subsec. (4) covers the CEMP: reviewed/updated annually, staff trained within 30 days of hire and annually, evacuation reported to the Regional Office within 6 hours and every 6 hours after, emergency shelter over-capacity reported within 48 hours. Subsec. (5) covers missing residents. Subsec. (6) covers incident reporting: Abuse Hotline immediately; APD Incident Reporting Form OP 3-0006 (Dec. 2025); initial notice of a critical incident within 4 hours and the completed form within 1 calendar day; reportable incidents within 1 calendar day; follow-up within 5 days.

citations.title: Siting; site selection of community residential homes
citations.requirement: No more than three APD facilities within 1,000 ft (rule subsec. (4)). Homes of 6 or fewer residents are a single-family use. Homes of 7-14 residents must be in multifamily zoning, and local government has 60 days to approve or deny. Notify zoning when the home receives its first resident.

citations.title: Personal Needs Allowance; Room and Board Payment
citations.requirement: The personal needs allowance is at least 18% of the SSI federal benefit rate ($178.92/month at the 2026 SSI rate of $994). APD room-and-board standard is $583.42/month. Claim room and board on Form 65G-13.008A within 90 days after month end.

citations.title: Medication administration training and validation
citations.requirement: Unlicensed staff may administer medication only after the APD Basic Medication Administration course (exam of at least 85%; 100% on the MAR section) and validation by an approved validator. They must complete an annual update and revalidation, and revalidate within the 60 days before expiry. Ch. 65G-7 is also incorporated by 65G-2.009(12)(e)-(f) for the daily medication record, storage and error reporting.

citations.title: Administration of medication
citations.requirement: An unlicensed direct service provider may supervise self-administration or administer oral, transdermal, ophthalmic, otic, rectal, inhaled, enteral or topical prescription medications only after an initial course of at least 6 hours by an agency-approved trainer. Validation is onsite with an actual client and medication, initially and annually, for oral, enteral, ophthalmic, rectal and inhaled routes. Otic, transdermal and topical routes are validated by simulation in the initial course. An annual 2-hour in-service on medication administration and error prevention is required. A provider who misses revalidation or the in-service must repeat the initial course. APD must set procedures by rule.

citations.title: Screening of direct service providers
citations.requirement: Level 2 employment screening under ch. 435 is required for direct service providers, managers and supervisors of licensed residential facilities, and anyone with access to residents' living areas, funds or property. Exemptions from disqualification only as provided in s. 435.07. Disqualifying offenses include those listed in the statute.

citations.title: Care Provider Background Screening Clearinghouse
citations.requirement: Screening results are managed through the AHCA Care Provider Background Screening Clearinghouse. Employers register and track eligibility there.

citations.title: Treatment of persons with developmental disabilities (Bill of Rights)
citations.requirement: Rights in subsec. (3) apply to all persons with developmental disabilities. They include dignity, privacy and humane care; freedom from abuse, neglect, exploitation and unnecessary restraint, isolation or excessive medication; religious freedom; social interaction and community participation; exercise and recreation; the right to consent to or refuse treatment, subject to a guardian advocate (s. 393.12) or guardian (ch. 744); and no discrimination in publicly funded programs. No behavioral program may be implemented unless reviewed under APD rule. Clients have the right to be free from unnecessary restraint or seclusion, and APD adopts rules limiting its use. Confirm the current subsection numbering against the 2025 statute.

citations.title: Reactive Strategies
citations.requirement: Providers that use reactive strategies need an APD-approved emergency procedure curriculum (65G-8.002): at least 12 direct training hours, a written test with an 80% minimum score, and certification valid for one year. Staff must be certified before using any technique. 65G-8.003 requires policies and procedures, an annual internal review and consent information in client records. 65G-8.008 covers chemical restraint. 65G-8.009 lists prohibited procedures. 65G-8.010 covers documentation and notification. Cited text is the 2008 adoption; APD has draft revisions in development, so confirm the current text before finalizing.

citations.title: Service Delivery Practice and Procedure - Behavior Analysis Services
citations.requirement: Behavior analysis services with restricted procedures are provided or supervised by a certified behavior analyst. Written plans go to the Local Review Committee (LRC) chair within 5 working days after implementation (65G-4.010(1)). The LRC reviews, approves or disapproves plans. Disapproved plans are revised and resubmitted within 14 working days (65G-4.008). Cited text is the 4/4/2012 rule; confirm current text.

citations.cite: Rule 59G-13.070, F.A.C. (iBudget Waiver Services Coverage and Limitations Handbook, May 2023)
citations.title: iBudget Waiver Services Coverage and Limitations Handbook
citations.requirement: Residential Habilitation (handbook pp. 2-46 to 2-65). Minimum direct-care hours per resident per 24 hours: Basic 2, Minimal 4, Moderate 6, Extensive 1 8, Extensive 2 11. The provider bills the monthly rate for 24 or more days in the home and the daily rate otherwise. Provider qualifications are on p. 1-20; Appendix B covers training and APD iConnect. Behavior focus and intensive behavioral designations (p. 2-48) require BCBA or Ch. 490/491 monitoring (p. 2-52) and staff training (pp. 2-52 to 2-53). The handbook requires the implementation plan, quarterly summary and annual report. The Medicaid Waiver Services Agreement is AHCA Form 5000-3553.

citations.title: iBudget Waiver Services Provider Rate Table
citations.requirement: Rates are set by support level and county group. The Oct. 1, 2025 table is incorporated; a July 2026 table (about +1.0% for residential habilitation) is in rule development (Notice 31315303).

citations.title: HCBS settings requirements
citations.requirement: Provider-owned or controlled residential settings need a lease or equivalent agreement, lockable bedroom doors, roommate choice, access to food and visitors, freedom to decorate, and documented person-centered justification for any modification (subsec. (c)(4)).

citations.title: Definitions
citations.requirement: A foster care facility has 3 or fewer residents. A group home facility has 4-15 residents. No new residential habilitation centers are licensed.

citations.title: Change of Ownership; License Violations (non-disciplinary and disciplinary); License Denial, Suspension or Revocation
citations.requirement: These rules, all effective 3/26/2026, govern change of ownership, violation classes and fines, and license denial, suspension or revocation. Chapter 65G-2 also repealed 65G-2.017 (Health Safety Standards) and 65G-2.014 effective 3/26/2026. Rule titles and effective dates are verified; read the full rule text before drafting detailed procedures.

citations.cite: s. 448.110, F.S.; Fla. Const. art. X, s. 24
citations.title: Florida Minimum Wage
citations.requirement: Florida minimum wage is $15.00/hour from Sept. 30, 2026.

citations.title: Workers' compensation definitions
citations.requirement: Workers' compensation coverage is required for employers with four or more employees.

citations.cite: ss. 39.201 and 415.1034, F.S. (as incorporated by Rule 65G-2.010(6)(a), F.A.C.)
citations.title: Mandatory reporting of abuse, neglect and exploitation
citations.requirement: Known or suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation is reported immediately to the Florida Abuse Hotline, 1-800-962-2873. The citation is verified as it appears in the text of 65G-2.010(6)(a); statute text was not independently fetched.

policies.category: 9. Supporting Documents – A. Documents to be provided with this application for residential facilities and adult training programs
policies.title: Comprehensive Emergency Management Plan (CEMP)
state_specifics: Written all-hazards CEMP using APD's CEMP template. Attach the local approval letter if a local authority approved it.
Covers residents who shelter in place, residents who are evacuated, and post-disaster activities including reporting relocated residents to the county emergency management office.
Update as needed and at least annually. Train all staff within 30 days of hire and annually after each update.
Report an evacuation to the APD Regional Office within 6 hours and every 6 hours after. Report emergency sheltering over capacity within 48 hours.

policies.category: 9. Supporting Documents – A. Documents to be provided with this application for residential facilities and adult training programs
policies.title: Behavioral Interventions and Responses to Behavioral Issues Involving Residents
state_specifics: Written policy on what direct service providers may do to prevent or respond to problematic behavior, including emergency procedures and reporting. It must be consistent with s. 393.13, ch. 65G-4 and ch. 65G-8.

Staff are trained to respond to serious, spontaneous behavioral incidents. Restraint, seclusion or physical-discomfort procedures are used only by staff certified under ch. 65G-8, with Local Review Committee approval.
Forbidden: physical or corporal punishment, verbal abuse, humiliation (including dark or locked time-out rooms), and any strategy prohibited by 65G-8.009.
Ch. 65G-8 certification requires an APD-approved curriculum of at least 12 direct hours, an 80% written test, and annual recertification.

policies.category: 9. Supporting Documents – A. Documents to be provided with this application for residential facilities and adult training programs
policies.title: Sexual Activity Policy Involving Residents
state_specifics: The licensee develops and enforces a written policy. It explicitly prohibits sexual activity between a resident and a covered person, and any sexual activity involving residents under 18. It must not abridge residents' civil and legal rights under s. 393.13.

Boundary standards: staff dress code; knocking before entering bedrooms; who may visit whose bedroom and when; separate beds for all residents and staff; bathing, showering and toileting assistance with no simultaneous bathing or toileting by staff; supervision guidelines; open reporting.
Train direct service providers on the policy.

For a sexually aggressive resident or one needing a Safety Plan: review history; review the Safety Plan and train staff before admission; resident or legal representative signs it and it is reviewed at least annually; APD approval before any shared bedroom.

policies.category: 9. Supporting Documents – B. Documents that must be provided with group home, foster care facility and residential habilitation center applications only
policies.title: Admission and Termination Criteria and Procedures
state_specifics: Written admission and termination criteria must match the resident characteristics (level of care, age, sex) on the license. Termination procedures must be consistent with ch. 65G-3.
Before placement: confirm it does not adversely affect current residents' health, safety or welfare.
Get APD approval before any placement that deviates from the licensure application criteria.
For a prospective resident who is not an APD client, give APD descriptive information: IDD documentation, medical needs, behavioral issues, known criminal history.
Notify APD before accepting each new resident and report the census change within 5 calendar days. APD reviews the home within 30 days after the first admission.

policies.category: 9. Supporting Documents – B. Documents that must be provided with group home, foster care facility and residential habilitation center applications only
policies.title: Video Monitoring Criteria and Protocols
state_specifics: Required only if cameras are used. Write criteria for which residents are monitored.
Written protocols: who may access footage; purpose and use of recordings; how, when and where footage is stored, with a minimum 30-day retention.
Consent, disclosure to APD and footage-preservation steps follow 65G-2.009(7)(b)3.-6.
Never use footage to humiliate or punish a resident.

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body and Facility Operator Responsibilities
state_specifics: Facility operator needs 90 college credits in a related field, or a high school diploma plus 3 years of disability experience.
Operator is on site or on call at all times, with a designated backup for absences.
Licensee employs adequate staff for the number and characteristics of residents, even above minimums (65G-2.008(1)).
Each home has its own license and operator assignment.

policies.title: Licensure, Certification and Provider Agreements
state_specifics: APD group home license (4-15 residents) or foster care facility (3 or fewer). One-year license, one license per home. APD will not fund an unlicensed facility.
Renew at least 45 days before expiration. Late or incomplete renewals are treated as initial applications. Give APD 30 days' written notice before closing a home.
Waiver enrollment: Provider Service Listing Letter, Medicaid enrollment, Medicaid Waiver Services Agreement (AHCA Form 5000-3553).
Fire inspection under ch. 69A-38 is needed before initial licensure and each renewal.
APD monitors at least monthly (one weekend visit a year) and reviews within 30 days after first admission.

policies.title: Policy Review and Document Control
state_specifics: Review the P&P manual at least annually, with the CEMP update.
Re-review when ch. 65G-2 changes (most rules amended 3/26/2026) and when the iBudget handbook or rate rules change.
Keep version history and staff acknowledgment of each revision.
Policies are submitted with the APD waiver provider packet and license application.

policies.title: Quality Improvement, Data Review and Mortality Review
state_specifics: Review incident reports (OP 3-0006), follow-up measures and trends at least quarterly.
Track medication errors, restraint use, elopements and injuries.
Review every death, using the death-notification steps. Specific mortality-review steps are not in the verified rules, so confirm current APD requirements.
Use findings from APD monthly monitoring visits in corrective action.

policies.title: Medicaid Compliance, Billing and Service Documentation
state_specifics: Bill only services covered by a WSC-issued authorization. Bill the monthly rate for 24 or more days in the home, otherwise the daily rate. Never bill days the resident was absent.
Rates follow Rule 59G-13.081 (by support level and county group). A July 2026 table is in rulemaking.
Document in APD iConnect; staff complete iConnect training (75% test).
Claim room and board on Form 65G-13.008A within 90 days after month end.
EVV in iConnect applies to personal care and home health, not residential habilitation.

policies.title: Financial Ability, Annual Cost Statement and Insurance
state_specifics: Keep proof of financial ability to operate. APD may ask for proof of ability to operate 60 days without state payment.
File the annual sworn statement of costs for APD-funded clients (s. 393.067(10)).
Workers' compensation is required with four or more employees (s. 440.02).
No minimum liability limit was found in rule. Carry liability and auto coverage and document it.

policies.title: Facility Siting, Zoning and Licensed Capacity Compliance
state_specifics: Six or fewer residents is a single-family use. 7-14 residents requires multifamily zoning, and local government has 60 days to approve or deny.
APD allows no more than three facilities within 1,000 ft.
Notify local zoning when the home receives its first resident.
Request capacity changes 30 days ahead with a passed fire inspection and zoning compliance.
Serve only residents whose characteristics match the license.

policies.title: Individual Rights and HCBS Settings Requirements
state_specifics: Protect rights under the s. 393.13 Bill of Rights: dignity, privacy, humane care; freedom from abuse, neglect, exploitation, unnecessary restraint, isolation and excessive medication.

Also: religious freedom, least restrictive conditions, education and training, social interaction and community activities, exercise and recreation, consent to or refuse treatment, non-discrimination, voting.
HCBS settings: lease or equivalent agreement, lockable bedroom doors, roommate choice, food access at any time, visitors, freedom to decorate.
Give residents and their representatives the Bill of Rights.

policies.title: House Rules
state_specifics: Written house rules and regulations are developed in consultation with residents and made available to residents and employees.
Rules cannot restrict HCBS rights (visitors, food access, privacy) without a documented person-centered modification.
Review rules with residents when they change and at admission.

policies.title: Rights Restrictions and Due Process
state_specifics: Any HCBS modification needs documented person-centered justification and informed consent.

No behavioral program is implemented unless reviewed under APD rule. Plans go to the Local Review Committee chair within 5 working days after implementation. Disapproved plans are revised and resubmitted within 14 working days.
Restraint and seclusion are limited by s. 393.13 and ch. 65G-8.
Residents and representatives are told how to challenge a restriction, with the grievance policy and Abuse Hotline.

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints
state_specifics: Residents may complain without retaliation.
Allegations of abuse, neglect or exploitation go to the Florida Abuse Hotline at 1-800-962-2873, not the internal grievance process.
Post the process in an accessible format; staff help residents file.
Log each complaint, response and outcome.

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
state_specifics: Records are stored securely in the home's designated office area (65G-2.0072(4)).
Release records only per HIPAA and s. 393.13. Give APD copies within 2 calendar days on request.
Protect resident privacy: bedroom and bathroom privacy, knocking before entering.
Video monitoring follows the video policy; footage is restricted.

policies.title: Personal Funds and Property Management
state_specifics: Written funds management and accounting procedures complying with GAAP. Train each staff member with access to resident funds or account information.
Personal needs allowance is at least 18% of the SSI FBR ($178.92/month at the 2026 rate of $994). Keep separate accounting for each resident.
Room and board standard is $583.42/month.
Keep a property inventory per 65G-2.009(3).
Monthly reconciliations signed by two staff, provided to residents and representatives.

policies.title: Informed Consent and Decision-Making Support
state_specifics: Residents have the right to consent to or refuse treatment, subject to a guardian advocate (s. 393.12) or guardian (ch. 744).
Keep consent information in the record, including consent to reactive strategies under 65G-8.003.
Obtain consent to the Safety Plan and video monitoring from the resident or legal representative.
Support residents to understand choices in plain language and make their own decisions where able.

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Communication Access
federal: Americans with Disabilities Act (42 U.S.C. 12101 et seq.)
state_specifics: No discrimination in publicly funded programs (s. 393.13).
Provide interpreters, communication devices and accessible formats at no cost.
Voting rights are protected and assistance offered.
Keep specialized equipment (65G-2.009(13)) in working order.

policies.title: Referral, Admission and Transition In
state_specifics: Referrals come from Waiver Support Coordinators and APD regional offices. Do not serve before a service authorization.
Apply the admission criteria in SDB-01 and notify APD before accepting each resident.
Review history and any Safety Plan before admission. Roommate matching needs APD approval where a Safety Plan applies.
Report the census change within 5 calendar days.

policies.title: Person-Centered Planning and the Individual Plan
state_specifics: Write an implementation plan for each resident with the resident, tied to support plan goals (iBudget Handbook, p. 2-48).
File quarterly summaries and an annual report with the support coordinator.
Record the resident's preferences, choices and any rights modifications.

policies.title: Implementation of Supports and Daily Documentation
state_specifics: Document each day's supports against the implementation plan.
Follow up on medical appointments (65G-2.009(1)).
Update resident records within 30 days of new information.
Enter documentation and authorizations in APD iConnect.

policies.title: Shift Communication and Staff Handoff
state_specifics: Written system to communicate recent incidents and resident information to staff on later shifts.
Document in writing medical or behavioral incidents and physician or therapist orders staff should know.
Procedure to ensure all shifts review it, with staff sign-off.

policies.title: Community Integration and Employment Choice
state_specifics: Provide opportunities for community activities (65G-2.009(2)).
Residents may take part in social interaction, exercise, recreation and community participation.
Support residents' choices about work and daily activities, including integrated employment.

policies.title: Transition, Discharge and Termination of Services
state_specifics: Follow the written termination procedures and ch. 65G-3.
Transfers need approval under 65G-2.009(3).
Report the census change to APD in writing before it occurs and update within 5 calendar days.
Return the resident's property per the inventory and personal funds per 65G-2.009(4).
Give 30 days' written notice to APD before closing a home.

policies.title: Medication Administration and Staff Certification
state_specifics: Administer only per the health care practitioner's written order, from original labeled containers, stored locked and accessible only to staff.
Keep a daily medication administration record per ch. 65G-7. Report errors and retrain staff after errors. Convey adverse reactions immediately to the prescriber.
Unlicensed staff need the APD Basic Medication Administration course (85% exam, 100% on the MAR section) and validation by an approved validator.
Annual update and revalidation within the 60 days before expiry. Annual 2-hour in-service on medication administration and error prevention (s. 393.506).

policies.title: Nursing Oversight and Health Care Coordination
state_specifics: Coordinate routine and specialty appointments and follow up on recommendations (65G-2.009(1)).
Share health changes with support coordinators, representatives and prescribers.
Residential habilitation is a non-nursing service. Use licensed nurses or providers for skilled needs.
Keep specialized equipment maintained (65G-2.009(13)).

policies.title: Health Monitoring, Seizures and Choking Risk
state_specifics: Individual health protocols (seizure, choking, aspiration) are part of each resident's plan.
At least one CPR-certified staff member on site whenever residents are present; classroom CPR/first aid within 90 days.
First aid per 65G-2.009(11).
Use modified diets and equipment as ordered.

policies.title: Change of Condition and Emergency Medical Care
state_specifics: At least one telephone accessible to staff and residents for emergency use at all times.
Post emergency numbers at each telephone extension, including each resident's doctors and support coordinator.
Report adverse medication reactions immediately to the prescriber.
Notify the legal representative and support coordinator of significant changes and report incidents under 65G-2.010(6).

policies.title: Death of an Individual
state_specifics: Call 911 and follow the resident's directives.
Report as a critical incident: initial notice to the APD Regional Office within 4 hours, Form OP 3-0006 within 1 calendar day. Confirm the death category under (6)(f)3.
Notify the legal representative and support coordinator.
Secure the resident's property and personal funds per the inventory and funds policy.
Update the census within 5 calendar days.

policies.title: Positive Behavior Support
state_specifics: Behavior analysis services with restricted procedures are provided or supervised by a certified behavior analyst.
Staff are trained on each resident's behavior plan by a certified behavior analyst, with the training documented in the personnel record.
Behavior focus homes: BCBA or Ch. 490/491 licensee monitoring and staff with 20 contact hours or RBT status; APD designation required.
Plans go to the Local Review Committee within 5 working days after implementation.

policies.title: Restrictive Interventions, Restraint and Seclusion
state_specifics: Restraint, seclusion and physical-discomfort procedures only by staff certified under ch. 65G-8 and with Local Review Committee approval.
Prohibited: corporal punishment, verbal abuse, humiliation, dark or locked time-out rooms, and procedures banned by 65G-8.009.
Chemical restraint is governed by 65G-8.008. Document and notify per 65G-8.010.
Annual internal review per 65G-8.003; confirm current text (APD revisions in development).

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
state_specifics: Report known or suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation immediately to the Florida Abuse Hotline: 1-800-962-2873.
Zero Tolerance training before providing services; refresher every 3 years.

If an employee has a verified finding and stays employed, submit a Corrective Action Plan to the Regional Office within 15 days: why not terminated, discipline, training and dates, how residents are protected.
Follow 65G-2.008(5) investigation rules for staff named as alleged perpetrators.

policies.title: Reportable Incidents and Investigations
state_specifics: Abuse, neglect, exploitation: immediately to the Abuse Hotline.
Critical incident: initial notice to the Regional Office within 4 hours; complete APD Incident Reporting Form OP 3-0006 within 1 calendar day.
Reportable incident: within 1 calendar day. Notify the legal representative and support coordinator.
Record follow-up measures on the form within 5 days. Incident types are listed in 65G-2.010(6)(f)3 and (g).
Cooperate with investigations and provide records promptly.

policies.title: Missing Person and Elopement
state_specifics: When a resident is determined missing, staff immediately call local law enforcement and get a case number.
If the officer declines a report, document the officer's name and contact the Watch Commander.
Make a critical incident report under 65G-2.010(6)(f): 4-hour notice, OP 3-0006 within 1 calendar day.
Keep current photo and identifying information in each resident's record. Elopement risk goes in the resident's plan.

policies.title: Residential Environment and Accessibility
federal: Americans with Disabilities Act (42 U.S.C. 12101 et seq.)
state_specifics: No mobile or manufactured homes. Maximum 2 residents per bedroom for homes first licensed on or after 7/1/2014.
Bedrooms: 80 sq ft single; 60 sq ft per person shared. One toilet, sink and tub/shower per 3 residents. 35 sq ft of living/dining space per household member.
Hot water at or below 120°F. Smoke and CO detectors. Restrict access to water hazards. Secure hazardous chemicals.
Designated office area with secure records storage.

policies.title: Emergency Preparedness and Fire Drills
state_specifics: Hold monthly fire drills. Record time of day, exits used, evacuation time and the signature of the person conducting. Keep records 1 year.
No drills between midnight and 5:00 a.m. Regional Office staff may observe drills.
Annual fire inspection under ch. 69A-38; approved inspection needed for licensure and renewal.
Facility is solely responsible for backup equipment or power and a plan for outages if a resident needs medically essential service (s. 366.15).
Follow the CEMP in SDA-01.

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
state_specifics: HIV/AIDS training for all staff within 90 days of hire.
Bloodborne pathogen exposure control plan, PPE and hepatitis B vaccine offer per OSHA.
The Florida Department of Health does not inspect APD-licensed homes. APD monitors compliance.
Sanitation, laundry, linens and waste handling as part of the homes' standards.

policies.title: Food, Nutrition and Modified Diets
state_specifics: Menus are planned, written and dated at least two days before consumption. Resident participation in meal planning is recommended.
Meals follow each resident's medical, behavioral and dietary requirements (65G-2.007(13)(e)).
Keep at least two days of fresh food and five days of staple food and drinking water on hand per the menu.
Residents have access to food at any time (HCBS settings).

policies.title: Transportation and Vehicle Safety
state_specifics: Staff who transport residents: valid license, no qualifying violation within 3 years, driving history updated annually.
Transportation standards per 65G-2.009(14).
Use wheelchair securement and seat belts as required.
Carry auto liability coverage and keep vehicle maintenance records.

policies.title: Staffing Ratios, Supervision and Awake Overnight Staff
state_specifics: At least one staff present at all times residents are in the facility. Leaving a resident alone for limited periods needs a written plan approved by the Regional Office before implementation.
Handbook minimum direct-care hours per resident per day: Basic 2, Minimal 4, Moderate 6, Extensive 1 8, Extensive 2 11. Multiply by residents at each level and meet the total daily or weekly.
Post a weekly staff schedule at least one week ahead. Keep actual schedules 6 months. Provide to the Regional Office within 3 calendar days on request.
Staff overnight per the resident's plan and risk; the rule requires presence at all times. Confirm any awake-overnight requirement in the individual plan or APD approval.

policies.title: Background Checks and Employee Registries
state_specifics: Level 2 screening via the AHCA Care Provider Background Screening Clearinghouse for the applicant, managers, supervisors and all direct service staff before they work.
Screening also covers anyone with access to residents' living areas, funds or property.
At least annually check the FDLE Sex Offender/Predator Database for registrants within one mile, notify staff and document the notification.
Track rescreening and eligibility in the Clearinghouse. Exemptions only as provided in s. 435.07.

policies.title: Direct Support Professional Qualifications and Hiring
state_specifics: DSPs are 18 or older with ch. 435 / s. 393.0655 screening, a high school diploma or equivalent, and 1 year of experience or 30 semester hours / 45 quarter hours / 720 classroom hours of related training.
Staff without experience may work under 90 days of supervision. Give written notice to the Regional Office within 5 days of hire and complete a performance evaluation within 120 days.
Required skills per 65G-2.008(3). Fitness for duty per 65G-2.008(4).

policies.title: Direct Support Professional Orientation and Training
state_specifics: Zero Tolerance before providing services; refresher every 3 years.
Direct Care Core Competencies, classroom CPR/first aid (no online-only) and HIV/AIDS within 90 days.
Behavior plan training by a certified behavior analyst. Comply with ch. 65G-8. Keep training documentation at least 3 years.
CEMP training within 30 days of hire and annually; medication administration certification before administering.

policies.title: Employee Health, Fitness for Duty and TB Screening
federal: Americans with Disabilities Act (42 U.S.C. 12101 et seq.)
state_specifics: Fitness for duty standards per 65G-2.008(4).
No TB testing requirement was found in ch. 65G-2 in the research. Follow employer policy and Department of Health guidance.
Keep health documents in a confidential file separate from the personnel file.
Offer the hepatitis B vaccine per OSHA.

policies.title: Personnel Records
state_specifics: Job descriptions for all paid staff.
Separate personnel record for each full and part-time employee: education, qualifications, experience, references, background screening, training participation, discipline.
Training documentation: dates, content, trainers, attendees. Retain training records at least 3 years.
Provide personnel records to the Regional Office within 3 calendar days on request.

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
state_specifics: Follow the boundary standards in the sexual activity policy (SDA-03).
Solicitation of residents is governed by 65G-2.009(10).
No physical or corporal punishment, verbal abuse or humiliation.
Staff may not borrow from or accept gifts from residents or use resident funds.

policies.title: Wage and Hour Compliance and Workers' Compensation
state_specifics: Florida minimum wage is $15.00/hour from Sept. 30, 2026.
Workers' compensation is required with four or more employees.
Pay overtime per the FLSA. Record time for all hours worked, including on-call and overnight.

policies.title: Individual Records and Retention
state_specifics: Keep resident records 6 years.
Update within 30 days of new information.
Copies to APD within 2 calendar days on request.
Store securely in the home's designated office area.

policies.title: Required Reports to the State
state_specifics: Census changes: written notice to APD before the change; updated census within 5 calendar days.
Critical incidents: 4 hours initial, OP 3-0006 within 1 calendar day. Evacuation: 6 hours and every 6 hours. Shelter over capacity: 48 hours.
Annual sworn cost statement (s. 393.067(10)). Renewal at least 45 days before expiration.
Capacity change requests 30 days ahead; closure notice 30 days; DSP supervised-hire notice within 5 days of hire.

documents.title: License Application (Group Home Facility / Foster Care / Residential Habilitation Center / ADT) – Section 9 Supporting Documents
documents.issuer: Florida Agency for Persons with Disabilities (APD)
documents.version: Posted APD copy footer reads 'month October' (Oct. 2025), 10 pages. A second posted file, 'APD Licensure Application_08-14-25', is a marked-up DRAFT (Jan. 2025/Oct. 2025). Rule 65G-2.002(2), as proposed on 1/6/2026, cites the 'December 2025' edition (flrules Ref-18971). I could not open that edition, so confirm it with the Regional Office.

Only the policy-content bullets are extracted; the Articles of Incorporation, employee roster, promotional materials, lease, fire inspection, financial evidence, budget sheet, prior-action documentation, capacity calculation/floor plan and zoning documentation are excluded as application paperwork.

required_items.text: Copy of Comprehensive Emergency Management Plan (CEMP) and the approval letter if the approval was made from a local authority
Policies and procedures regarding behavioral Interventions and Responses to behavioral Issues Involving residents.
Applicant's or Licensee's written policy regarding sexual activity involving residents of the facility
required_items.cite: APD Form 65G-2.002-A, §9.A (the Aug. 2025 draft adds 'or participants')

required_items.text: Written criteria and procedures in place for the admission or termination of residential services for residents
required_items.cite: APD Form 65G-2.002-A, §9.B (group home, foster care, RHC applications only)

required_items.text: Written criteria relating to the use of video monitoring equipment if applicant makes use of such devices

The licensee shall have written criteria and procedures in place for the admission or termination of residential services for clients; termination procedures must be consistent with Chapter 65G-3, F.A.C. (the 2026 notice prints '(a) No change'; text taken from the prior rule.)

When determining whether to accept a person as a resident, the facility shall: 1. ensure placement does not adversely affect the health, safety, or welfare of current residents; 2. obtain the Agency's approval prior to any placement that deviates from the criteria on the licensure application; 3. provide descriptive information to the Agency on a prospective resident who is not an Agency client (IDD documentation, medical needs, behavioral issues, known criminal history).

Resident rights: the facility shall adhere to and protect resident rights and freedoms under the Bill of Rights of Persons with Developmental Disabilities (s. 393.13, F.S.), including: 1. dignity, privacy, humane care, freedom from abuse/neglect/exploitation; 2. freedom from harm, including unnecessary physical, chemical or mechanical restraint, isolation, excessive medication; 3. religious freedom; 4. services in the least restrictive conditions; 5. education and training; 6. social interaction and community activities; 7. exercise and recreation; 8. consent to or refuse treatment; 9. non-discrimination; 10. voting.

Each facility shall establish, maintain, and make available to residents and employees written house rules and regulations in consultation with residents, for the orderly operation of the group home facility.

The licensee must develop policies and procedures which detail the methods for management and accounting of any personal funds or benefits of facility residents. The policies and procedures must comply with generally accepted accounting principles. Each staff member having access to resident funds and account information must be trained in the proper implementation of these policies and procedures.

Only if a resident is to be left alone for limited periods: the licensee prepares a written plan proposing that a specified client be left alone for limited periods during the day or night; the plan must be approved by the Regional Office prior to implementation.

A licensee who uses video monitoring shall: 1. develop written criteria for determining which residents will be monitored by video camera; 2. develop written protocols for implementing video monitoring, including a. who may access video footage, b. the purpose and use of video recordings, and c. how, when, and where footage will be stored and for how long, to include a minimum thirty-day retention period. (See also (7)(b)3.-6. on consent, disclosure to the Agency and footage preservation.)

The facility shall have a written statement of policies and procedures governing actions that may be taken by direct service providers to help prevent or respond to problematic behaviors exhibited by residents, including emergency procedures and reporting requirements, consistent with s. 393.13, F.S., and Chapters 65G-4 and 65G-8, F.A.C.

Direct service providers must be trained to appropriately respond to serious and spontaneous behavioral incidents requiring emergency intervention; restraint/seclusion or physical-discomfort procedures only if certified under Chapter 65G-8 and with Local Review Committee approval; forbidden responses: 1. physical or corporal punishment; 2. (no change); 3. verbal abuse; 4. humiliation (including dark or locked time-out rooms); 5. any reactive strategy prohibited under Rule 65G-8.009.

The licensee shall develop and enforce a written policy regarding sexual activity involving residents of the facility. Such policy shall: 1. explicitly prohibit sexual activity between a resident and a covered person; 2. explicitly prohibit sexual activity involving residents under age eighteen; 3. not abridge residents' civil and legal rights (s. 393.13, F.S.); 4. address appropriate physical boundaries and standards among direct service providers and residents, including: a. dress code for direct service providers; b. mutual respect for personal space (e.g., knocking before entering a bedroom); c. parameters on who is allowed to visit whose bedroom and under what conditions; d. all residents and direct service providers sleep in separate beds; e. assisting/supervising bathing, showering, toileting, and no simultaneous bathing/toileting by staff; f. guidelines on level and type of supervision; g. open communication to encourage reporting of inappropriate sexual behavior.

The licensee shall provide direct service providers with training regarding the sexual-activity policy. Safeguards must be implemented in any facility serving one or more sexually aggressive residents or residents requiring a Safety Plan (review of history information; Safety Plan review before admission and staff training; resident or legal representative signs the Safety Plan and it is reviewed at least annually; Agency approval before sharing a bedroom; no unsupervised closed-door contact for minors; bathroom use one at a time; no obscene materials for minors).

[Standard; the notice text does not use the words 'written policy'] Medication: administration per the health care practitioner's written order; original labeled containers; locked storage accessible only to staff; daily medication administration record per Chapter 65G-7; administration, documentation, storage and error reporting per ss. 393.13 and 393.506, F.S., and Chapter 65G-7; ongoing staff re-training when medication errors occur; adverse reactions conveyed immediately to the prescriber or medical professional.

Each facility shall have a system in place to communicate recent incidents and resident information to staff on subsequent shifts, including 1. a mechanism for documenting in writing information (medical or behavioral incidents, physician or therapist orders) staff should know, and 2. a procedure to ensure the information is reviewed across all shifts.

At least one telephone accessible to direct service providers and residents for emergency use at all times; required emergency telephone numbers (including each resident's doctors and each resident's support coordinator) readily accessible at each telephone extension.

Emergency preparedness drills: dates and results of required monthly fire drills (time of day, points of exit used, evacuation time, signature of person conducting) recorded and kept one year; no fire drills between midnight and 5:00 a.m.; Regional Office staff may observe drills. (Annual fire inspection under Chapter 69A-38, F.A.C., is required under 65G-2.010(2).)

Each facility shall prepare and maintain a written comprehensive emergency management plan (s. 393.067(8), F.S.), updated as needed and annually, addressing: 1. provisions for all hazards (hurricanes, tornadoes, flooding, fires, hazardous materials, transportation accidents, power outages in severe cold/hot weather); 2. care of residents remaining in the facility (pre-disaster preparation, protecting the facility, supplies, medications, emergency power, food and water, adequate staffing, emergency equipment); 3. care of residents evacuated (identification of residents, transfer of records, evacuation transportation, sheltering, supplies, staffing, emergency equipment, medications); 4.-5. [printed as 'No change', not shown in the notice]; 6. post-disaster activities (family inquiries, medical intervention, transportation, reporting relocated residents to the county emergency management office); 7. [printed as 'No change', not shown]. Staff must be trained on the plan within 30 days of hire and annually after each update.

Missing residents procedure: after determining that a resident is missing, staff immediately call local law enforcement and ask the officer to [items (a) and (c) printed as 'No change'], assign a case number; if the officer refuses a report, document the officer's name and contact the Watch Commander; make a critical incident report per (6)(f).

Incident reporting: known or suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation reported immediately to the Florida Abuse Hotline (ss. 39.201, 415.1034, F.S.); critical incidents — initial notice to the Regional Office within four hours and a complete APD Incident Reporting Form (OP 3-0006) within one calendar day; reportable incidents within one calendar day; notify the legal representative and support coordinator; follow-up measures on the form within five days; list of critical and reportable incident types in (6)(f)3. and (6)(g).
All licensees with employees shall develop and maintain the following personnel policies, procedures and records: (a) Job descriptions for paid staff
Documentation of all facility staff training, including a record of training dates, training content and trainers, and staff in attendance

Separate personnel records for each full and part-time employee that contain written documentation of the employees' education, qualifications experience, references, background screening, staff training participation, and any disciplinary action taken against the employee

A weekly written schedule indicating staff coverage for at least one week in advance. Weekly schedules of actual staff coverage shall be maintained for a six-month period (provide to the Regional Office within three calendar days on request, (6)(b)).

Staff training requirements: Zero Tolerance training (detection, prevention, reporting of abuse, neglect, exploitation) before providing direct services, with a refresher every three years; basic first aid and CPR certification within 90 days (classroom, not online; at least one CPR-certified provider on site when residents are present); staff trained on residents' current behavior plans by a certified behavior analyst, with documentation in the personnel record; comply with Chapter 65G-8; written documentation of required training kept at least three years.

Safety standards: annual update of staff driving history for staff who transport residents; at least annually access the FDLE Sex Offender/Predator Database for registrants within a one-mile radius, notify staff and document the notification.

If an employee has a verified finding of abuse, neglect, exploitation or abandonment and remains employed, the licensee must submit a Corrective Action Plan to the Regional Office within 15 days containing: 1. why the employment is not terminated; 2. disciplinary action taken; 3. any training and dates; 4. how residents will be protected.

Menus shall be planned, written, and dated at least two days in advance of consumption. Resident participation in meal planning is recommended but not required. (Also (13)(e): meals are developed in accordance with residents' individual medical, behavioral, and dietary requirements; (13)(g): at least two days of fresh food and five days of staple food and drinking water supplies on hand in accordance with the menu.)

Each facility that requires medically essential service is solely responsible for any backup equipment or power supply and a planned course of action in the event of a power outage or interruption of service, in accordance with s. 366.15, F.S.

sections: 9. Supporting Documents – A. Documents to be provided with this application for residential facilities and adult training programs (policy items only: CEMP; behavioral interventions policies and procedures; sexual activity policy)

9. Supporting Documents – B. Documents that must be provided with group home, foster care facility and residential habilitation center applications only (admission/termination criteria and procedures; video monitoring criteria)

official.notes: No standalone APD policy-review checklist for group homes was located. An older version of Rule 65G-2.002 told staff to review applications using a 'Group Home Facility Checklist APD 2014-04' <cite index="8-1">(10) Agency staff shall review applications for licensure using the following forms: Foster Care Facility Checklist APD 2014-03... Group Home Facility Checklist APD 2014-04</cite>. The 2025–26 rule instead requires the license application <cite index="9-1">All applications for initial licensure as well licensure renewal must be submitted using License Application form 65G-2.002-A</cite>, whose Section 9 is the working checklist. Submission: the application is completed under oath and sent to the APD Regional Office, with renewals due at least 45 days before expiration <cite index="9-2">An application for the renewal of license must be submitted to the Agency at least 45 days prior to the expiration of the current license.</cite>. The application is complete only on receipt of all required documents, screening results and fees, and a licensure inspection is not authorized until then (proposed 65G-2.002(11)-(12)). APD's iConnect new-licensing guide lists attachments including <cite index="7-6,7-7,7-8,7-9">Admin Policies; Emergency Mgmt Plan; Professional Liability Insurance; Sexual Activity Policy</cite>, so also upload policies as separate, clearly titled files. Suggested organization: use the form's order (9.A, then 9.B) for the five form items, then a rule-based section keyed to the rule citations above (resident rights/house rules, resident funds, behavior, sexual activity, video monitoring, medication, emergency/fire, incident and missing-resident reporting, personnel and training, meals). Cross-reference each manual section to its form bullet or rule number. Caveats: (1) the form's two bullet lists are unnumbered, so 'bullet N' IDs are my own counting; (2) the rule items other than 65G-2.007 use numbering from the Jan. 6, 2026 proposed text and may differ in the adopted 3/26/2026 text; I confirmed this for 65G-2.007, where the adopted menu item is (13)(f) rather than the proposed (13)(g); (3) the Oct. 2025 form still shows the older 'residents of the facility' wording on the sexual-activity bullet, and the proposed rule text refers to a December 2025 edition, so confirm the current edition with the Regional Office. Not listed as written-policy items because the rule text does not call for a written policy: records content (resident records, property inventory, transportation log), solicitation permission, first aid kit, and optional in-service training. Form Section 4 also asks the applicant to attest that all employees receive abuse-prevention training before direct client contact. The rule text reviewed contains no explicit requirement for written complaint/grievance, theft/loss or control-of-property procedures. Check iBudget Handbook/MWSA provider requirements (Rule 59G-13.070) separately for waiver enrollment, which these documents do not cover.
